text: Our talk on canalization and noise won the Best Student Presentation Award (3rd place) at CCS 2026, Binghamton.
Talk at NetSci 2026 on canalization and robustness under noise.
Joined the CBeRa ERA Chair group of Prof. Luis M. Rocha at the Católica Biomedical Research Centre, Lisbon, as a Research Fellow.
Talk at NetSci 2025, Maastricht: canalization and symmetry enhance noise resilience in the density classification task.
Started my PhD in Systems Science at Binghamton University, after an MS there (2023–2024).
Poster at NetSci 2024, Québec City: Monopoly as a random walk on a weighted network.
